stations.challenge: Your friend wants to plan every day, but you don’t. Suggest a plan for the first week.
followUpQuestions: What is the first thing you do when the holidays start?
How do you feel when school finishes for the summer?
What would you do with a completely free day?
stations.mainQuestion: How do you want to spend the first week?
stations.stretch: Describe your perfect first week: what you do each day and why.
stations.subtitle: No school for two months!
stations.title: The First Day of the Holidays

stations.challenge: You have seven days and only a little money. Plan a holiday together.
followUpQuestions: Do you like the sea, the mountains or cities more?
Where would you like to go in summer?
What is interesting to see in your town or region?
stations.mainQuestion: Do you prefer travelling or staying at home?
stations.stretch: Compare a holiday abroad with a holiday at home. Give two good points for each.
stations.subtitle: The sea, the mountains or home?
stations.title: Travel or Stay at Home?

stations.challenge: Your friends are going on a trip, but one friend can’t come. What can you do?
followUpQuestions: Who do you like spending summer with?
What did you do with your friends last summer?
When do you like being alone? Why?
stations.mainQuestion: Where do you meet your friends in summer?
stations.stretch: Plan a day for you, a friend and someone from your family. What can you all enjoy?
stations.subtitle: Summer with other people
stations.title: Friends and Family

stations.challenge: Choose: four weeks in a shop or two weeks helping at an animal shelter. Explain your choice.
followUpQuestions: Would you like a summer job?
What could you learn in a summer job?
What would you buy with your money?
stations.mainQuestion: What would be a good holiday job?
stations.stretch: Your friend wants to work all summer. Give two reasons for and two reasons against.
stations.subtitle: Work or free time?
stations.title: Summer Jobs and Money

stations.challenge: Your group wants a weekend without screens, but one friend says no. Make two simple rules together.
followUpQuestions: What games do you play with friends in summer?
How much time do you spend on your phone?
What can you do without a screen?
stations.mainQuestion: Would you try a day without your phone?
stations.stretch: Make a list of five summer activities without screens and choose the best one.
stations.subtitle: Online or offline?
stations.title: Phones and Games

stations.challenge: Your friend thinks everyone else has a better summer. Give your friend two tips.
followUpQuestions: What is the most boring part of summer for you?
Is it OK to do nothing all day? Why?
What do you do to feel better when you are bored?
stations.mainQuestion: How do you relax on a rainy day?
stations.stretch: Describe a quiet summer day that you really enjoyed.
stations.subtitle: Doing nothing is OK.
stations.title: Boring Days and Rest

stations.challenge: Tell a short summer story in one minute. Your partner asks two questions.
followUpQuestions: What was a really fun summer day for you?
What food reminds you of summer?
What photo would you show a friend?
stations.mainQuestion: Tell your partner about a summer surprise.
stations.stretch: Your partner tells your story back to you. What did they forget?
stations.subtitle: Your best summer days
stations.title: Summer Memories

stations.challenge: Say two good things and two bad things about long summer holidays.
followUpQuestions: How do you feel the night before school starts?
What is the best thing about going back to school?
What would you like to do next summer?
stations.mainQuestion: What will you miss most about summer?
stations.stretch: Plan your next summer: one thing to learn, one place to visit and one person to see.
stations.subtitle: The end of the holidays
stations.title: Back to School

vocabulary.explanation: a place where people stay in tents
put things in a bag for a trip
work for a few hours a day or a week
red, painful skin after too much sun
feel happy about something in the future

warmUp.note: If you want: a short activity to start.
warmUp.prompt: Pick three summer activities and explain which you like best and why.

ui.lessonGoal: Say what you think and give simple reasons.
ui.levelTip: Choose 4 stations. Prepare your question before you speak.

presentation.introduction: Two months without school! Travel, friends, family, rest, money. What do you like about summer? Talk about it with a partner.
presentation.privacyNotice: You can invent examples. You don’t need to talk about your family, money or private plans.
quickStart: Give a reason or an example.
Need more? Open the next task.
presentation.strap: What do you do in summer?
presentation.subtitle: A conversation, not a test
